heard: On one asteroid, the sun rises and sets in completely random locations. Discovered on January 4, 1989, 4179 Tautates is nearly five kilometers long. On September 29, 2004, this massive space rock passed within four lunar distances of our planet. Internet rumors at the time falsely claimed the asteroid carried a high chance of hitting Earth. Later observations by the Chinese probe Chang2 revealed it is a gingerroot shaped contact binary. Instead of a stable spin, tautates tumbles through space like a football after a botch pass. This chaotic rotation explains precisely why on one asteroid, the sun rises and sets in completely random locations.
